extracted.intended_audience: registrants, corporate issuers, and securities counsel preparing SEC registration statements and reports (Regulation S-K/Securities Act filings)
extracted.subtask_short: SEC registration statement undertakings and exhibits
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and compliance rules for disclosure, undertakings, and exhibits to be included in Securities Act registration statements and related reports (Regulation S-K Items 510–601). Covers indemnification disclosure, expense itemization, a range of post-effective undertakings, exhibit filing/indexing and redaction procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of contingent basis, interest, or connection
rubrics_metrics.description: If any principal underwriter (or other specified persons) has a contingent basis, interest, or connection, furnish a brief statement of the nature of such contingent basis, interest, or connection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicable to underwriters, voting trustees, directors, officers, or employees; statement should be brief and describe the nature of the contingency/interest/connection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert/counsel interest de minimis threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: The interest of an expert (other than an accountant) or counsel will not be deemed substantial and need not be disclosed if the interest...does not exceed $50,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For this Instruction the term 'expert or counsel' includes the firm, corporation, partnership or other entity by which such expert or counsel is employed or of which he is a member or of counsel to and all attorneys in the case of counsel, and all nonclerical personnel in the case of named experts, participating in such matter on behalf of such firm, corporation, partnership or entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountant qualification/disqualifying interests (Instruction to Item 509)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accountants providing a report on the financial statements presented or incorporated by reference should note § 210.2-01 of Regulation S-X regarding 'Qualification of Accountants' which discusses disqualifying interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants must follow Regulation S-X when considering disqualifying interests of accountants whose reports are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of Commission position on indemnification for Securities Act liabilities (Item 510)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the undertaking required by paragraph (h) of Item 512 is not required to be included and waivers comparable to those in paragraph (h) have not been obtained, include a brief description of indemnification provisions relating to directors, officers and controlling persons against liability arising under the Securities Act, together with a specified statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the standardized statement: 'Insofar as indemnification for liabilities arising under the Securities Act of 1933 may be permitted ... such indemnification is against public policy as expressed in the Act and is therefore unenforceable.' Follow Item 702 of Regulation S-K for additional disclosure. Also include related underwriting agreement indemnification provisions where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Itemized statement of other expenses of issuance and distribution (Item 511)
rubrics_metrics.description: Furnish a reasonably itemized statement of all expenses in connection with issuance and distribution of the securities to be registered, other than underwriting discounts and commissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any securities are offered for the account of security holders, indicate the portion of such expenses to be borne by the selling security holder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction to Item 511 — specific expense items and estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Insofar as practicable, registration fees, Federal taxes, State taxes and fees, trustees' and transfer agents' fees, costs of printing and engraving, and legal, accounting, and engineering fees shall be itemized separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include as a separate item any premium paid by the registrant or any selling security holder on any policy obtained in connection with the offering which insures or indemnifies directors or officers. Information may be given as subject to future contingencies; if amounts are unknown, give estimates identified as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undertaking to file post-effective amendments during offers/sales (Rule 415 offerings) (Item 512(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: If securities are registered pursuant to Rule 415, the registrant undertakes to file, during any period in which offers or sales are being made, a post-effective amendment to the registration statement to: (i) include any prospectus required by section 10(a)(3) of the Securities Act; (ii) reflect in the prospectus any facts or events arising after the effective date which constitute a fundamental change; and (iii) include any material information with respect to the plan of distribution not previously disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: paragraphs (a)(1)(i) and (ii) do not apply to Form S-8 when the information is contained in periodic reports incorporated by reference; (i),(ii),(iii) do not apply to certain S-1/S-3/SF-3/F-3 filings when information is contained in incorporated reports or in prospectuses filed pursuant to §230.424(b). For asset-backed securities forms, Item 1100(c) may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deeming post-effective amendments as new registration statements (Item 512(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of determining any liability under the Securities Act, each such post-effective amendment shall be deemed to be a new registration statement relating to the securities offered therein, and the offering of such securities at that time shall be deemed to be the initial bona fide offering thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule affects timing/liability treatment for issuers and underwriters when offering changes are filed post-effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undertaking to remove unsold securities on termination (Item 512(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Undertake to remove from registration by means of a post-effective amendment any of the securities being registered which remain unsold at the termination of the offering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrant must file the post-effective amendment to remove unsold securities at offering termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign private issuer filing of financial statements for delayed/continuous offerings (Item 512(a)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant is a foreign private issuer, undertake to file a post-effective amendment to include any financial statements required by Item 8.A of Form 20-F at the start of any delayed offering or throughout a continuous offering, unless such information is contained in reports incorporated by reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial statements and information otherwise required by Section 10(a)(3) need not be furnished provided the registrant includes such financial statements by post-effective amendment so that all prospectus information is at least as current as the date of those financial statements. Exceptions for Form F-3 where incorporated periodic reports suffice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability treatment of prospectuses under Rules 430B, 430C, and 430D (Item 512(a)(5)-(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: If relying on Rule 430B/C/D, each prospectus filed pursuant to specified subsections shall be deemed part of the registration statement as of specified dates (e.g., the date first used after effectiveness or date of first contract of sale) for liability purposes; specific rules govern which prospectuses are 'part of' the registration statement and how that affects effective date and liability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The provision includes caveats that no statement made later will, as to purchasers with earlier contract dates, supersede or modify statements made prior to such effective date; consult the specific subparagraphs for distinctions among 430B, 430C, and 430D and applicable prospectus filing types (§230.424(b)(2),(b)(3),(b)(5),(b)(7), etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrant deemed a 'seller' for liability when certain communications are used (Item 512(a)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of determining liability to any purchaser in the initial distribution, the registrant undertakes that it will be a seller to the purchaser and considered to offer or sell the securities if the securities are offered or sold to such purchaser by means of: (i) any preliminary prospectus or prospectus required by Rule 424; (ii) any free writing prospectus prepared by or on behalf of the registrant or used or referred to by the registrant; (iii) the portion of any other free writing prospectus containing material information about the registrant provided by or on behalf of the registrant; and (iv) any other communication that is an offer in the offering made by the registrant to the purchaser.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This undertaking clarifies which communications create registrant liability as a seller regardless of underwriting method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special filing obligation for Form SF-3 when relying on §230.430D (Item 512(a)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant is relying on §230.430D with respect to any offering of securities registered on Form SF-3, undertake to file the information previously omitted from the prospectus filed as part of an effective registration statement in accordance with §§ 230.424(h) and 230.430D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures omitted information is filed in the manner and timing required by 430D/424(h) for SF-3 shelf offerings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filings incorporating subsequent Exchange Act documents by reference are deemed new registration statements (Item 512(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registration statement incorporates by reference any Exchange Act document filed subsequent to the effective date, the registrant undertakes that each filing of the registrant's annual report pursuant to section 13(a) or 15(d) that is incorporated by reference shall be deemed to be a new registration statement relating to the securities offered therein, and the offering of such securities shall be deemed the initial bona fide offering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This affects liability/timing whenever post-effective Exchange Act filings are incorporated by reference into a registration statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form S-4/F-4 resale reoffering prospectus content and filing undertakings (Item 512(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: If securities are being registered on Form S-4 or F-4 in connection with a Rule 145 transaction, the registrant undertakes that before any public reoffering by any person who may be deemed an underwriter, such reoffering prospectus will contain the information called for by the applicable registration form regarding reofferings by persons who may be deemed underwriters, in addition to other required information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also undertakes that every prospectus filed pursuant to paragraph (h)(1) or that purports to meet section 10(a)(3) and is used in connection with a Rule 415 offering will be filed as part of an amendment and not used until such amendment is effective; for liability purposes each such post-effective amendment with a prospectus is deemed a new registration statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceleration/filing-effective-upon-filing: indemnification disclosure & judicial submission procedure (Item 512(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: If acceleration of the effective date is requested or if a Form S-3/F-3 will become effective upon filing or if registration is on Form S-8, and (1) any provision exists whereby the registrant may indemnify directors/officers/controlling persons against Securities Act liabilities, or (2) underwriting agreement contains such a provision, and (3) benefits not waived, then include specified disclosure and the standardized unenforceability statement; if a claim is asserted the registrant will, unless settled by controlling precedent, submit to a court the question whether such indemnification is against public policy and be governed by final adjudication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the standard unenforceability paragraph and follow the described court-submission procedure if a claim for indemnification (other than payment of expenses in successful defense) is asserted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 430A omitted information & post-effective amendment treatment (Item 512(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: For registration statements permitted by Rule 430A, the registrant undertakes that: (1) information omitted from the form of prospectus filed in reliance on Rule 430A and contained in a later prospectus filed pursuant to Rule 424(b)(1) or (4) or 497(h) shall be deemed part of the registration statement as of the time it was declared effective; and (2) each post-effective amendment that contains a form of prospectus shall be deemed a new registration statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affects liability and timing when using Rule 430A omitted information procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualification of trust indentures — trustee eligibility application (Item 512(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant intends to rely on section 305(b)(2) of the Trust Indenture Act of 1939 to determine eligibility of the trustee for delayed offerings, the registrant undertakes to file an application to determine trustee eligibility under the Commission's rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow rules/regulations prescribed under section 305(b)(2) for trustee eligibility determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asset-backed offerings incorporating third-party Exchange Act documents deemed new registration statements (Item 512(k))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registration statement incorporates by reference any Exchange Act document filed subsequent to the effective date pursuant to Item 1100(c) of Regulation AB, the registrant undertakes that each filing of the annual report of a third party incorporated by reference shall be deemed to be a new registration statement relating to the securities offered therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies specifically to asset-backed securities and Item 1100(c) incorporation by reference rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibits and exhibit index required; hyperlink and placement requirements (Item 601(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to Rule 411(c) and Rule 12b-23(c) regarding incorporation of exhibits by reference, exhibits required in the exhibit table must be filed as part of the registration statement or report. Each registration statement or report shall contain an exhibit index which must appear before the required signatures. Each exhibit identified (other than certain eXBRL exhibits) must include an active link to the exhibit filed with the registration statement or, if incorporated by reference, an active hyperlink to the separately filed exhibit on EDGAR. If amended, each amendment must include hyperlinks to the exhibits required with the amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See paragraph (b) for descriptions of exhibits; exhibit filing timing and incorporation-by-reference are governed by referenced rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material contracts and amendments — filing as exhibits (Item 601(a)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a material contract or plan of acquisition, reorganization, arrangement, liquidation or succession is executed or becomes effective during the reporting period reflected by a Form 10-Q or Form 10-K, it shall be filed as an exhibit to the Form 10-Q or Form 10-K filed for the corresponding period. Any amendment or modification to a previously filed exhibit to a Form 10, 10-K or 10-Q shall be filed as an exhibit to a Form 10-Q and Form 10-K, unless not currently required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A required exhibit may be incorporated by reference from a previous filing where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedules to exhibits — when not required and obligations if omitted (Item 601(a)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedules (or similar attachments) to the exhibits required are not required to be filed provided they do not contain information material to an investment or voting decision and that information is not otherwise disclosed in the exhibit or disclosure document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each filed exhibit must contain a list briefly identifying the contents of all omitted schedules. Registrants need not prepare a separate list if the information is included within the exhibit. Registrant must provide a copy of any omitted schedule to the Commission or its staff upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redaction of exhibits for personal privacy/confidentiality (Item 601(b)(2) / paragraph (b)(2)(ii) guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The registrant may redact specific provisions or terms of exhibits required to be filed if the registrant customarily and actually treats that information as private or confidential and if the omitted information is not material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If redacting, mark the exhibit index to indicate portions omitted; include a prominent statement on the first page of the redacted exhibit that certain identified information has been excluded because it is not material and is treated as private or confidential; include brackets showing where information is omitted. If requested by the Commission or staff, promptly provide an unredacted copy and materiality and privacy/confidentiality analyses; registrant may request confidential treatment of supplemental material while in the Commission's possession pursuant to §200.83. Commission may require amendment to include previously redacted information if its analyses are insufficient. Follow §230.418 or §240.12b-4 procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction: preliminary immaterial exhibit changes need not be refiled (Instruction 1 to Item 601)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an exhibit filed in preliminary form has been changed only to insert immaterial information such as interest, dividend or conversion rates, redemption or conversion prices, purchase or offering prices, underwriters' or dealers' commissions, names, addresses or participation of underwriters, or to correct typographical errors or insert signatures, the registrant need not refile the exhibit as amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any such incomplete exhibit may not, however, be incorporated by reference in any subsequent filing under any Act administered by the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction: one copy of substantially identical exhibits with schedule of omissions (Instruction 2 to Item 601)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where two or more indentures, contracts, franchises or other documents required to be filed as exhibits are substantially identical in all material respects except as to parties, dates of execution or other details, the registrant need file a copy of only one such document, with a schedule identifying the other documents omitted and setting forth the material details in which they differ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission may at any time require filing of copies of any documents so omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction: copies rather than originals required (Instruction 3 to Item 601)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only copies, rather than originals, need be filed of each exhibit required except as otherwise specifically noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow specific form/rule notes where originals are expressly required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction: designation for exhibits filed in paper or as confirming electronic copy under hardship exemptions (Instruction 4 to Item 601)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever an exhibit is filed in paper pursuant to a hardship exemption, the letter 'P' (paper) shall be placed next to the exhibit in the list of exhibits. Whenever an electronic confirming copy of an exhibit is filed pursuant to a hardship exemption, the exhibit index should specify where the confirming electronic copy can be located; in addition, the designation 'CE' (confirming electronic) should be placed next to the listed exhibit in the exhibit index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies when hardship exemptions under §§232.201 and 232.202 are used for exhibit filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit table use and meaning of 'X' designation (Instructions to Exhibit Table)
rubrics_metrics.description: The exhibit table indicates documents that must be filed as exhibits to the respective forms listed. The 'X' designation indicates the documents which are required to be filed with each form even if filed previously with another document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previously filed documents may, however, be incorporated by reference to satisfy the filing requirements where permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit list — specific required exhibits (Exhibit Table items 1–107)
rubrics_metrics.description: The exhibit table enumerates specific exhibits (e.g., (1) Underwriting agreement; (2) Plan of acquisition, reorganization, arrangement, liquidation or succession; (3)(i) Articles of incorporation; (3)(ii) Bylaws; (4) Instruments defining rights of security holders; (6) [Reserved]; (7) Correspondence from independent accountant regarding non-reliance; (8) Opinion re tax matters; (9) Voting trust agreement; (10) Material contracts; (13) Annual report to security holders, Form 10-Q; (14) Code of Ethics; (15) Letter re unaudited interim financial information; (16) Letter re change in certifying accountant; (17) Correspondence on departure of director; (18) Letter re change in accounting principles; (19) Insider trading policies; (20) Other documents/statements to security holders; (21) Subsidiaries; (22) Subsidiary guarantors; (23) Consents of experts and counsel; (24) Power of attorney; (25) Statement of eligibility of trustee; (31)-(32) certifications; (33)-(36) asset-backed related exhibits; (95) Mine Safety Disclosure Exhibit; (96) Technical report summary; (97) Policy Relating to Recovery of Erroneously Awarded Compensation; (98) de-SPAC reports/opinions; (99) Additional exhibits; (101)-(107) interactive/asset data files and filing fee table).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Which forms require each exhibit is indicated by the table. Use the table to determine exhibit requirements for specific filing forms (S-1, S-3, SF-1, SF-3, S-4, S-8, S-11, F-1, F-3, F-4, 10, 8-K, 10-Q, 10-K, ABS-EE, etc.). Many items are reserved; refer to the exhibit table for exact applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of Exhibit (1): Underwriting agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each underwriting contract or agreement with a principal underwriter pursuant to which the securities being registered are to be distributed; if terms not determined, the proposed forms thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such agreement may be filed as an exhibit to a Form 8-K which is incorporated by reference into a registration statement subsequent to its effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of Exhibit (2): Plan of acquisition, reorganization, arrangement, liquidation, or succession
rubrics_metrics.description: Any material plan of acquisition, disposition, reorganization, readjustment, succession, liquidation, or arrangement and any amendments thereto described in the statement or report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrant may redact specific provisions or terms of exhibits required by paragraph (b)(2) if the information is customarily treated as private or confidential and not material; if redacted, mark exhibit index and include prominent statement and brackets; provide unredacted copy and analyses to Commission on request; may request confidential treatment per §200.83; Commission may require filing previously redacted information if analyses inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of Exhibit (3)(i): Articles of incorporation — filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The articles of incorporation of the registrant or instruments corresponding thereto as currently in effect and any amendments thereto must be filed. Whenever the registrant files an amendment to its articles, it must file a complete copy of the articles as amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the amendment is reported on Form 8-K, only the text of the amendment need be filed as an exhibit; a complete copy of the amended articles must be filed as an exhibit to the next Securities Act registration statement or periodic report to which the exhibit requirement applies. If impracticable to file a charter amendment authorizing new securities before the effective date, the registrant may file the form of amendment to be filed with the state authority; if material changes are made after the copy is filed, the registrant must file the changed copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of Exhibit (3)(ii): Bylaws — filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The bylaws of the registrant or instruments corresponding thereto as currently in effect and any amendments thereto must be filed. Whenever the registrant files an amendment to the bylaws, it must file a complete copy of the amended bylaws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such bylaw amendment is being reported on Form 8-K, the registrant is required to file only the text of the amendment as a Form 8-K exhibit; otherwise file the full amended bylaws as required by the applicable registration statement or report.
